statement: Rosa and Omar start together at the same point of a $400$-meter running track and run around it in the same direction. Rosa runs $200$ meters per minute and Omar runs $250$ meters per minute. How many complete laps has Rosa run at the moment Omar first passes her?

choices.misconception: I divided the track length by Rosa's speed, 400 / 200 = 2, but that is how many minutes her first lap takes, not a number of laps.
I worked out the moment correctly but gave Omar's number of laps instead of Rosa's.
I found that Omar passes Rosa after 8 minutes and gave the minutes instead of the laps.
I found that Rosa has run 4 laps and Omar 5 laps, and added them to get 9 instead of giving only Rosa's laps.

hints: To pass Rosa, Omar must get a whole lap, $400$ meters, ahead of her.
Omar gains $250 - 200 = 50$ meters on Rosa every minute. How long until he has gained $400$ meters?
He is a full lap ahead after $400 / 50 = 8$ minutes. How far has Rosa run by then?

solutions.reliable: Omar first passes Rosa when he has run exactly one lap more than she has. He gains $50$ meters per minute, so this happens after $400 / 50 = 8$ minutes. By then Rosa has run $200 \cdot 8 = 1600$ meters, which is $4$ laps, and Omar has run $2000$ meters, which is $5$ laps.
solutions.elegant: Their speeds are in the ratio $200 : 250 = 4 : 5$, so whenever Rosa has run $4$ laps Omar has run $5$. That is the first time Omar is exactly one lap ahead.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
